 The Nasdaq-100 Is Doing Something It Did Only in 2000 and 2018. Here’s What Happened Next Both Times
 By Jeremy Phillips 
 Published November 17, 2026, 9:51pm ET · 2 min read 
 𝕏 
 f 
 ⧉ 
 Quick Read
 QQQ closed 13.5% below its October 6 record on Tuesday, its third 10% drop from a record in 2026.
 Since QQQ began trading in 1999, only 2000 and 2018 also had three or more such drops in one year.
 A year after first crossing a 10% drop from a record, QQQ was higher in 9 of 14 cases.

 A retiree who had $250,000 in the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ: QQQ) at its October 6 record has about $216,199 today.
 QQQ, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, closed at $656.95 on Tuesday, 13.5% below its record close of $759.66 on October 6. It first closed 10% below that record on November 2.
 That makes three times in 2026 that QQQ has fallen 10% or more from a record high. It first did it on March 27, then July 29, and now November 2. Each of the first two drops ended with a new record within a few months.
 In our count from QQQ's daily closes since it began trading in 1999, only two other years had three or more of these drops: 2000 and 2018. The S&P 500 has fallen much less this time: the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is 6.0% below its own record.
 How 2000 and 2018 ended
 2000: QQQ had 4 drops of 10% from a record that year. The last one, which began in late March, never recovered: QQQ eventually fell 83% and did not close at a new high again until 2016.
 2018: QQQ had 3. The third began in late August and reached 23.2% by late December. QQQ was back at a record by April 17, 2019, and was up 18.3% a year after that drop first crossed 10%.
 A year later
 Across every 10% drop from a record since 1999 with a full year of data after it, QQQ was higher 12 months after first crossing the 10% line in 9 of 14 cases. Every miss came from 2000 or 2022.
 Those counts start at QQQ's first close 10% below a record. Between 2000 and 2016 QQQ never closed at a new high, so no new drops from a record could start in those years.
 Where this one stands
 QQQ's lowest close in this drop so far was 14.8% below the October record. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), one of its largest holdings, was up after hours on Tuesday after reporting results, as we reported . We also looked at how much Nvidia's selloff cost a $10,000 QQQ position .
